title: Fabrication of a Functionalized Magnetic Bacterial Nanocellulose with Iron Oxide Nanoparticles
protocol: Prepare 500 ml of liquid culture medium by combining yeast extract, peptone, mannitol, and high purity water.
Autoclave the liquid culture medium at 120 °C for 20 min.
Store the autoclaved liquid culture medium at 4 °C.
Prepare 100 ml of semisolid media by adding agar to yeast extract, peptone, mannitol, and high purity water.
Autoclave the semisolid mixture at 120 °C for 20 min.
Deposit 5 ml of the autoclaved semisolid mixture in a plastic Petri dish.
Allow the solution to gel at 4 °C.
Store the gelled Petri dishes at 4 °C until further use.
Rehydrate G. xylinus strain preserved in freeze-dried vials by adding liquid culture medium and pipetting up and down, as indicated by the manufacturer's instructions.
Inoculate Petri dishes containing semisolid media with small droplets of bacterial suspension using an inoculating loop.
Move the inoculating loop in a zig zag direction from the edge to the center of the dish.
Incubate the Petri dishes at 26 °C for 72 hours in an incubator without CO2.
Store the Petri dishes at 4 °C by sealing the lid with Parafilm and placing the dishes upside down if not immediately used.
Transfer 2 ml of liquid culture medium into each well of a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Take two colonies from inoculated Petri dishes using an inoculating needle and place them into the first well of the tissue culture plate.
Repeat the procedure for the remaining 23 wells.
Incubate the tissue culture plate at 30 °C for 7 days.
Collect BNC pellicles from the growth media.
Sterilize BNC pellicles in 200 ml of 1% NaOH solution for 1 hr at 50 °C.
Optionally, stir the NaOH solution at 300 rpm using a magnetic bar and stirring plate.
Discard the NaOH solution after sterilization.
Add 200 ml of freshly prepared 1% NaOH solution to BNC pellicles.
Repeat the sterilization process until BNC pellicles in solution acquire a translucent appearance.
Rinse BNC pellicles with water three times.
Store BNC pellicles in high purity water at room temperature, ensuring they are completely submerged and do not dry out.
Autoclave BNC pellicles at 121 °C for 20 min.
Bubble 1,000 ml of high purity water with nitrogen gas to remove dissolved oxygen.
Use a three-neck round bottom flask to prepare a solution in a 2:1 molar ratio of iron(III) chloride hexahydrate and iron(II) chloride tetrahydrate diluted with deoxygenated high purity water.
Weigh 5.4 g of FeCl3·6H2O and 1.98 g of FeCl2·4H2O in 10 ml of deoxygenated high purity water, or use 0.54 g of FeCl3·6H2O and 0.198 g of FeCl2·4H2O in 20 ml if the solution becomes too viscous.
Close the three-neck round bottom flask with septum stoppers until it is connected to the nitrogen gas supply and condenser tube.
Connect the nitrogen gas supply to a needle punched in a septum stopper and fixed to one neck of the vessel, and use another neck for output.
Place 1 BNC pellicle prepared previously (15.6 mm diameter and 2-3 mm thickness) in the vessel with reactants, ensuring it is completely submerged in liquid.
Connect the remaining neck of the vessel to a condenser tube.
Add a drying tube filled with anhydrous calcium sulfate on top of the condenser tube.
Run water through the condenser tube.
Seal all glass joints with vacuum grease.
Heat the solution in a silicone oil bath to 80 °C using a stirring hotplate.
Stir the reactants at 350 rpm for 5 min.
Increase the stirring velocity to 700 rpm.
Add 5 ml of ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH, 14%) to the solution in intervals of 5 min.
Continue stirring the solution at 80 °C for another 5 min.
Lower the temperature of the solution to 30 °C using the temperature control bottom of the stirring hotplate.
Stir the mixture for another 5 minutes at 30 °C.
Turn off the hot plate after stirring.
Cool the mixture down to room temperature (RT).
Separate magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) and bacterial nanocellulose (BNC) using a strong permanent magnet.
Transfer the mixture to a vessel flask.
Hold MNPs and BNC in place with the magnet while decanting the supernatant.
Resuspend the MNPs and BNC in 100 ml of water.
Gently shake the solution to remove non-strongly incorporated MNPs.
Decant the supernatant again by holding MNPs and BNC in place using the magnet.
Wash the MNPs and BNC several times with deoxygenated high purity water until the supernatant reaches neutral pH (pH ~7).
Separate the magnetic-functionalized bacterial nanocellulose (MBNC) from the MNPs using tweezers.
Rinse the MBNC several times with water until it runs clear.
Sterilize the MBNC by exposing it to UV light (110-280 nm) overnight.
Autoclave 500 ml of deoxygenated high purity water at 120 °C for 20 min and store the MBNC in 20 ml of this water.
Immerse the sample in 1% PEG and stir for 2 hr at RT (37 °C).
Mount samples on the indentation using glue for nanoindentation testing.
Perform normal loading and unloading nanoindentation test using a Berkovich indenter with a radius of 20 nm.
Calibrate contact area as a function of indentation depth at RT using fused silica and tungsten.
Approach the samples in their thickness direction during testing.
Randomly select indentation locations on sample surfaces, keeping spacing between indentations between 200-300 mm.
Apply load to samples in steps and record corresponding displacement of the indenter.
Analyze plot of load vs depth to find Young's modulus.
Carry out the nanoindentation test.
Apply load rates between 0.0001 mN/sec and 0.005 mN/sec.
Use peak loads between 0.01 mN and 0.60 mN.
Conduct tests in a liquid cell with deionized water (DI water).
Lyophilize samples for 24 hours at -80 °C.
Mount lyophilized samples on SEM studs.
Sputter coat samples with Au-Pd film for 10 seconds.
Analyze nanocellulose fiber structure using scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Take images at magnifications of 22,000X and 60,000X.
Use an acceleration voltage of 5 kV during SEM analysis.
Allow MBNC pellicles to completely dry at room temperature (RT).
Expose dried MBNC pellicles to a permanent magnet for 5 minutes.
Conduct magnetic force measurements using bio-AFM according to manufacturer's protocol.
Capture topography features first with the bio-AFM in non-contact mode.
Acquire magnetic domains during a second pass with the bio-AFM in non-contact mode.
Characterize magnetic nanoparticles using vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM).
Perform VSM characterization within a physical property measurements system (PPMS) from Quantum Design.
Conduct VSM analysis at room temperature (300 K).
Apply a magnetic field ranging between -10,000 and 10,000 Oe for VSM measurement.
Seed human aortic smooth muscle cells in a 6-well tissue culture plate at a density of 1.0x103 cells/cm2.
Incubate the seeded cells for 24 hours.
Add test samples: BNC and MBNC pellicles to the incubated cells.
Use untreated cells as negative controls.
Treat control cells with hydrogen peroxide to serve as positive controls.
Perform the Comet assay according to manufacturer's protocols.
Intercalate and fluorescently label DNA in the electrophoresed samples using SYBR Gold.
Analyze cells for fluorescent round green nucleoids indicating no DNA damage.
Identify long comets in samples indicating DNA damaged cells.
